Alert.description:

polite `role="status"`.

AsyncContent.description:
Loading, error and empty states for remote content (a post list, a gallery, a product grid), so
every list handles them the same way. Renders no wrapper element.

error.description: Any truthy value shows the error state (an `Error`'s message is shown by default).

isEmpty.description: Show the empty state (checked after loading and error).

loadingFallback.description: Shown while loading. Default: a centred `Spinner`. Pass skeletons shaped like the content for less layout shift.

errorFallback.description: Shown on error. Default: a danger `Alert` with the message and, with `onRetry`, a "Try again" button.

emptyFallback.description: Shown when `isEmpty`. Default: a plain `EmptyState` titled "Nothing here yet".

onRetry.description: Retry handler for the default error state.

children.description: The loaded content, or a function so it's only evaluated once the data is there.

examples:
<AsyncContent isLoading={isLoading} error={error} isEmpty={posts?.length === 0} onRetry={refetch}
  loadingFallback={<Skeleton height={120} />}>
  {() => posts!.map(post => <PostCard key={post.id} post={post} />)}
</AsyncContent>

ButtonGroup.description:
Groups related buttons. Attached by default; set `attached={false}` for a
spaced toolbar row.

Card.description:
A raised surface for grouping related content. Compose with `CardHeader`,
`CardContent` and `CardFooter`. Set `href` (and `as` for a router link) to make
the whole card a link, or `as="button"` to make it a button.

variant.description: `interactive` adds hover elevation for clickable cards; `inset` gives a sunken background. Defaults to `interactive` when `href` is set or the card renders a `<button>`.

padding.description: Inner padding. `none` is useful for media or tables that run edge to edge. Default `md`. Accepts a breakpoint object.

fill.description: Stretch to 100% height of its grid cell or flex container, with CardFooter pinned to the bottom. Works with `href` and `as="button"`.

href.description:
Makes the whole card a link (renders an `<a>`, or router link; always a plain `<a>` with
`download` or a `target` other than `_self`). Do not nest other links or buttons inside.

as.description:
Element or component to render, e.g. `as="article"`, a router link with `href`, or `as="button"` for a
selectable card (it gets `type="button"` and loses the browser's button styles).

examples:
<Card fill>
  <CardHeader><Heading level={4}>Usage</Heading></CardHeader>
  <CardContent>…</CardContent>
  <CardFooter>…</CardFooter>
</Card>
<Card href="/pricing"><Heading level={3}>Pricing</Heading></Card>
<Card as="button" aria-pressed={selected} onClick={select}>Album</Card>

  {reviews.map(r => <CarouselSlide key={r.id}><Card>…</Card></CarouselSlide>)}
</Carousel>

CookieConsent.description:
Cookie consent banner with accept all / reject non-essential / customise.
Choices are saved in localStorage and exposed through `useCookieConsent`.

in line with GDPR / PECR guidance. Only load non-essential scripts once
`consent[category]` is true.

categories.description: Cookie categories. Default: necessary (required), analytics, marketing.

description.default: 'We use essential cookies to make this site work, and optional cookies to understand how it is used. You can choose which optional cookies to allow.'

policyHref.description: Link to your cookie or privacy policy.

storageKey.description: localStorage key for the saved choices. Default `field-cookie-consent`.

version.description: Bump this when your categories change to ask everyone again. Default `1`.

layout.description: `bar` spans the bottom of the screen; `card` floats in a corner. Default `bar`.

onChange.description: Called with the choices whenever the visitor saves them.

examples: <CookieConsent policyHref="/cookies" onChange={c => c.analytics && loadAnalytics()} />

Divided.description:
Several parts sharing one surface (a card, a panel, a band), separated by hairlines instead of
each getting its own box. The outer edges get no extra space, so the parts line up with the
container's padding. Line colour: `--field-divided-color`.

direction.description:
`column` (default) stacks the parts with horizontal lines between them; `row` puts them side by
side (equal width unless `columns` is set), with vertical lines. Accepts a breakpoint object, e.g. `{ base: 'column', md: 'row' }`.

space.description:
Space on each side of a line (number = px, `$6` = spacing token). Default `$6` (24px). Accepts a
breakpoint object, e.g. `{ base: '$6', md: '$8' }` for 24px stacked and 32px side by side.

columns.description:
Column widths while the parts are side by side, as a `grid-template-columns` value, e.g.
`'3fr 2fr'` for a 60/40 split. Default equal widths. Ignored while stacked; accepts a breakpoint object.

as.description: Element to render. Default `div`.

padding.description: Padding (number = px, `$4` = spacing token); accepts a breakpoint object.

hideBelow.description: Hide below this breakpoint (e.g. `hideBelow="md"` shows only from 768px).

hideFrom.description: Hide from this breakpoint up (e.g. `hideFrom="md"` shows only below 768px).

examples:

  <Divided direction={{ base: 'column', md: 'row' }}>
    <Stack gap="$2">…opening hours…</Stack>
    <Stack gap="$2">…admission…</Stack>
    <Stack gap="$2">…getting here…</Stack>
  </Divided>
</Card>

asChild.description: Merge the link styles onto the single child element.

as.description: Render as a router link, e.g. `as={NextLink}`.

external.description: Opens in a new tab with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, adds an icon and a screen-reader hint.

Gallery.description: A grid of image tiles that open in a full-screen `Lightbox`.

columns.description: Columns; accepts a breakpoint object. Default `{ base: 2, md: 3 }`.

gap.description: Gap between tiles. Accepts px number, token or breakpoint object. Default `8`.

lightbox.description: Open a full-screen `Lightbox` when a tile is clicked. Default `true`.

lightboxProps.description:
Passed to the Gallery's `Lightbox`, e.g. toolbar `actions`:
`lightboxProps={{ actions: image => <LightboxAction … /> }}`.

previewCount.description:
Show only the first N photos, with a "Show all" button; accepts a breakpoint object, e.g.
`{ base: 6, md: 9 }`. Hidden photos are still in the lightbox.

showAllLabel.description: Custom label for the expand button when `previewCount` is set.

isLoading.description: Display skeleton placeholders while images are loading.

skeletonCount.description: Number of skeletons to render when `isLoading` is true. Default 6.

examples: <Gallery images={photos} columns={{ base: 2, lg: 4 }} ratio={4 / 3} />

Grid.description:
CSS grid. Use `minChildWidth` for card grids that reflow on their own, or a
breakpoint object on `columns` for explicit control.

columns.description: Number of equal columns, or any `grid-template-columns` value. Accepts a breakpoint object, e.g. `{ base: 1, md: 2, lg: 3 }`.

minChildWidth.description: Responsive auto-fit: columns at least this wide (e.g. `240` or `"16rem"`), as many as fit. Takes precedence over `columns`.

gap.description: Space between cells. Default 16px (`$4`). Accepts a breakpoint object.

align.description: Vertical alignment of items within their row (`align-items`): the same values as `Flex align`. Default `stretch`; accepts a breakpoint object.

as.description: Element to render. Default `div`.

padding.description: Padding (number = px, `$4` = spacing token); accepts a breakpoint object.

hideBelow.description: Hide below this breakpoint (e.g. `hideBelow="md"` shows only from 768px).

hideFrom.description: Hide from this breakpoint up (e.g. `hideFrom="md"` shows only below 768px).

examples:
<Grid minChildWidth={260} gap={16}>{cards}</Grid>
<Grid columns={{ base: 1, md: 2, lg: 3 }} gap="$6">{features}</Grid>

Heading.description:
Section heading. `level` sets the size; pass `as` to decouple the visual
size from the semantic tag, e.g. `<Heading level={1} as="h2">`. Use `display`
for hero-sized headlines. Headings use the theme's `--field-font-display`.

level.description: Visual size and, by default, the rendered `h1`-`h4` tag. Default 2.

display.description:
Large, fluid display size for hero and section headlines (`sm` to `xl`). Scales with the
viewport and overrides the size implied by `level` (the tag still follows `level` / `as`).

align.description: Text alignment; accepts a breakpoint object.

as.description: Render a different tag than the level implies (keep the document outline correct while choosing the look).

examples: <Heading level={1} display="lg" align={{ base: 'start', md: 'center' }}>Fresh bread, every morning</Heading>

Icon.description:
A theme-coloured, sized icon. Decorative by default (hidden from screen readers); give it a
`label` when the icon is the only thing conveying the meaning.

icon.type: ElementType<any, keyof IntrinsicElements> | ReactElement<any, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>>
icon.description: The icon: a component such as Lucide's `MapPin`, or an element (`<MapPin />`).

tone.description: Colour from the theme. Default `inherit` (the surrounding text colour).

label.description: Accessible name. Without it the icon is decorative and hidden from screen readers.

inline.description: Sit the icon on the text baseline, for an icon before a few words in a sentence.

examples:
<Icon icon={MapPin} tone="accent" />
<Icon icon={AlertTriangle} tone="warning" label="Warning" />

IconButton.description:
A square, icon-only button. `aria-label` is required so the action is
announced to assistive technology.

icon.description: The icon to render, e.g. `<Settings size={16} />`.

aria-label.description: Required: icon-only buttons need a text label for screen readers.

children.description: With `asChild`, pass the element to render (e.g. a `<Link>`) as the child.

asChild.description: Merge this component's props and styling onto its single child element instead of rendering its own (use with router `<Link>`s).

as.description: Render as a different element or component, e.g. `as={Link}`.

href.description:
Render as an anchor (or the `ThemeProvider` router link for internal paths). With `download` or
a `target` other than `_self` it is always a plain `<a>`.

examples: <IconButton icon={<Trash2 size={16} />} aria-label="Delete" variant="ghost" />

IconText.description:
An icon beside a block of text: an address, opening hours, a feature list item. The icon is
decorative; the text carries the meaning.

icon.type: ElementType<any, keyof IntrinsicElements> | ReactElement<any, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>>
icon.description: The icon: a component such as Lucide's `Clock`, or an element.

gap.description: Space between the icon and the text (number = px, `$3` = spacing token). Default `$2.5` (10px).

align.description: Align the icon with the first line of text (`start`, default) or centre it on the whole block.

as.description: Element to render. Default `div`.

examples:
<IconText icon={MapPin}>
  <Text weight="semibold">RAF Snaith Museum</Text>
  <Text tone="secondary">Pollington, East Yorkshire</Text>
</IconText>

Image.description: Responsive image with optional aspect-ratio cropping, rounded corners, caption and an error fallback. Lazy-loads by default; pass `priority` or `loading="eager"` for above-the-fold heroes. Works with `srcSet` / `sizes` like a normal ``.

alt.description: Describe the image; pass `""` for purely decorative images.

ratio.description: Crop to a fixed aspect ratio (e.g. `4 / 3`). Without it the image keeps its natural shape.

fit.description: How the image fills a fixed ratio. Default `cover`.

position.description: Focal point when cropping, e.g. `"center top"`.

radius.description: Corner radius from the theme. Default `md`.

priority.description:
Load first: for the above-the-fold hero or the Largest Contentful Paint image. Sets
`loading="eager"` and `fetchpriority="high"` (in the spelling your React version accepts).

fallback.description: Shown if the image fails to load. Defaults to an icon on a neutral background.

examples: <Image src="/img/latte.jpg" alt="Latte art in a ceramic cup" ratio={4 / 3} priority caption="Our house blend" />

Lightbox.description:
Full-screen image viewer with previous/next, captions, a counter, arrow-key and swipe
navigation. Used by `Gallery`; render it yourself for custom triggers.

onClose.description: Called when the user asks to close it (Escape, backdrop click or close button).

actions.description:
Extra controls for the toolbar, rendered before Close and inside the focus trap. Called with the
image shown and its index, so the controls change as the user steps through. Use `LightboxAction`
so they match Close.

aria-label.description: Accessible name of the dialog. Default `Image viewer`.

LightboxAction.description:
An icon control for `Lightbox` `actions`, styled like the viewer's Close button. A button by
default; a link with `href`.

`download` only saves same-origin files: for files on another domain the browser opens them
instead, so add `target="_blank"` to keep the viewer open.

aria-label.description: Required: the control has no visible text.

href.description: Render as a link. With `download` or `target` it is always a plain `<a>`, never the router link.

as.description: Render as a different element or component.

examples: <LightboxAction icon={<Download size={20} />} aria-label="Download poster" href={image.src} download target="_blank" />

Link.description: Inline text link for body copy, footers and legal text.

tone.description: Colour: `accent` (default), `inherit` from the surrounding text, or `subtle` (secondary text).

underline.description: Underline behaviour. Default `always`, which keeps links distinguishable in body copy.

external.description: Opens in a new tab with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, adds an icon and a screen-reader hint.

as.description: Render as a router link, e.g. `as={NextLink}`.

asChild.description: Merge the link styles onto the single child element.

examples:
<Text>Read our <Link href="/privacy">privacy policy</Link>.</Text>
<Link href="https://maps.google.com/?q=..." external>Get directions</Link>

Meter.description:
Shows a measurement within a known range (disk usage, quota), turning amber
and red past the thresholds.

label.description: Visible label, linked to the control for screen readers.

valueLabel.description: Text on the right of the header. Defaults to the percentage.

warningThreshold.description: Percentage at which the bar turns amber. Default 75.

dangerThreshold.description: Percentage at which the bar turns red. Default 90.

examples: <Meter label="Disk" value={412} max={500} valueLabel="412 / 500 GB" />

Modal.description:
A centred dialog that blocks the page. Traps focus while open, restores it
to the trigger on close, locks page scroll and closes on Escape/backdrop.

onClose.description: Called when the user asks to close it (Escape, backdrop click or close button).

footer.description: Action row, typically Cancel + primary action buttons.

footerLayout.description: Layout for footer buttons: `actions` (row, right-aligned) or `stack` (full-width stacked column). Default `actions`.

aria-label.description: Accessible name when there is no visible `title`.

closeOnBackdropClick.description: Close when the backdrop is clicked. Default `true`.

closeOnEscape.description: Close when Escape is pressed. Default `true`.

initialFocusRef.description: Element to focus when opened. Defaults to the first focusable element.

container.description: Element to render into. Defaults to `document.body`.

examples:
<Modal isOpen={open} onClose={() => setOpen(false)} title="Delete bucket?"
  footer={<><Button onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Cancel</Button><Button variant="danger">Delete</Button></>}>
  This permanently removes all objects.
</Modal>

Navbar.description:
Responsive top navigation bar. Compose with `NavbarBrand`, `NavbarContent`
(holding `NavbarItem`s and `NavbarFlyout`s), `NavbarActions`, `NavbarToggle` and
`NavbarMenu` (the mobile drawer). Set `variant` + `animated` for a sliding
active indicator.

sticky.description: Stick to the top of the scroll container.

floating.description: Detached, rounded "island" style with margins (implies sticky).

scrollBehavior.description: Effect applied once the page scrolls past `scrollThreshold`: add elevation, shrink the bar, or blur the background.

scrollThreshold.description: Scroll distance in px before `scrollBehavior` / `transparentOnTop` change state.

scrollContainerRef.description: Element to watch for scrolling instead of `window` (e.g. a scrollable `<main>`).

transparentOnTop.description:
Transparent background until the page is scrolled (it turns solid while the mobile menu is open).
`true` is always transparent at the top. `'auto'` is only transparent while the page has a band
under the bar: a `Section underNavbar`, or any element with `data-navbar-overlap`. Pages
without one (loading, error and not-found states) get a solid bar.

maxWidth.description: Max width of the inner content (`sm` 640px … `xl` 1280px, `full`, or any length).

collapseBelow.description:
Switch to the mobile layout (`NavbarToggle` shown, `hideOnMobile` content hidden) while the
navbar is narrower than this: `sm` 640px … `xl` 1280px or a px number. Use it when many
top-level items need more room than the default. The built-in 768px collapse always applies.

isMenuOpen.description: Controlled open state of the mobile `NavbarMenu`.

defaultMenuOpen.description: Initial mobile menu state when uncontrolled.

onMenuOpenChange.description: Called when the mobile menu opens or closes.

variant.description: Default indicator style for every `NavbarContent`: `underline`, `elastic` (fluid stretch), `pill`, `rail` or `ghost` (no indicator).

animated.description: Animate the active indicator between items.

glow.description: Soft accent glow on the active indicator.

hoverGlider.description: A spotlight that follows the pointer across items.

indicatorWidth.description: `full` item width, `content` (text width only), a px number or a % string.

height.description:
Height of the bar (e.g. `68` or `"4.25rem"`). Default 56px, or 48px when compact. Sets
`--field-navbar-height` on the bar; a sticky, floating or `transparentOnTop` bar also sets it on
`<html>`, where `Section underNavbar`, the anchor scroll offset and your own CSS can read it.
For server-rendered pages, also set it in CSS (`:root { --field-navbar-height: 68px }`) so the
first paint is right.

mode.description: Force dark or light mode for the navbar without needing a separate ThemeScope wrapper.

theme.description: Explicit theme or theme pair to apply directly to the navbar.

navLabel.description: Accessible name of the inner `<nav>` landmark. Default "Main".

as.description: Render as a different element or component, e.g. `as={Link}`.

examples:
<Navbar sticky blurred variant="elastic">
  <NavbarBrand href="/">Acme</NavbarBrand>
  <NavbarContent>
    <NavbarItem href="/" isActive>Overview</NavbarItem>
    <NavbarItem href="/billing">Billing</NavbarItem>
  </NavbarContent>
  <NavbarActions><NavbarToggle /></NavbarActions>
  <NavbarMenu>…mobile links…</NavbarMenu>
</Navbar>

NavbarActions.description:
Right-aligned slot for utility buttons (search, theme toggle, avatar, `NavbarToggle`).
Wrap a single child in `NavbarActionsItem hideOnMobile` to hide just that one on phones.

gap.description: Space between children (number = px, `"$4"` = spacing token).

hideOnMobile.description: Hide the whole group while the bar is in its mobile layout. Hide single children with `NavbarActionsItem`.

NavbarActionsItem.description:
One child of `NavbarActions` that can be hidden on its own while the bar is collapsed,
e.g. a "Book tickets" button that moves into `NavbarMenu` on phones. Without `asChild` it
renders a `display: contents` wrapper, so it doesn't affect the actions' layout.

hideOnMobile.description: Hide this child while the bar is in its mobile layout (below 768px or `collapseBelow`).

asChild.description: Merge the props onto the single child instead of rendering a wrapper.

examples:
<NavbarActions>
  <NavbarActionsItem hideOnMobile asChild><Button href="/tickets">Book</Button></NavbarActionsItem>
  <NavbarToggle />
</NavbarActions>

NavbarBrand.description:
Logo / product name slot. Renders a link when `href` is set: the `ThemeProvider` `linkComponent`
for internal paths, or your own component via `as` / `asChild`.

href.description: Render as a link (`<a>`) pointing at this URL.

asChild.description: Merge this component's props and styling onto its single child element instead of rendering its own (use with router `<Link>`s).

as.description: Render as a different element or component, e.g. `as={Link}`.

NavbarContent.description:
Group of navigation items. Owns the animated active indicator: the item with
`isActive` is tracked and the indicator slides between items on change.

align.description: Where this group sits in the bar.

gap.description: Space between children (number = px, `"$4"` = spacing token).

variant.description: Indicator style for this group (overrides the `Navbar` default).

indicatorWidth.description: `full` item width, `content` (text width only), a px number or a % string.

glow.description: Soft accent glow on the indicator.

hoverGlider.description: A spotlight that follows the pointer across items.

hideOnMobile.description: Hide this group below the mobile breakpoint (put the links in `NavbarMenu` instead).

NavbarFlyout.description:
A dropdown / mega-menu panel opened from a navbar trigger. Becomes an inline accordion inside `NavbarMenu` on mobile.
The panel closes when a link inside it is clicked, on Escape (focus returns to the trigger),
on an outside click, and when keyboard focus leaves it.

onOpenChange.description: Called with the new open state.

align.description: Preferred panel alignment relative to the trigger. The panel shifts sideways as needed to stay within the navbar and viewport.

gap.description: Space between children (number = px, `"$4"` = spacing token).

NavbarFlyoutItem.description: A rich link card (icon, title, description, badge) for use inside a `NavbarFlyout`.

icon.description: Icon element, e.g. `<Server size={16} />` from lucide-react.

badge.description: Small count or status shown on the right.

href.description: Render as a link (`<a>`) pointing at this URL.

asChild.description: Merge this component's props and styling onto its single child element instead of rendering its own (use with router `<Link>`s).

as.description: Render as a different element or component, e.g. `as={Link}`.

NavbarItem.description: A top-level navigation link or button. Mark the current route with `isActive` (sets `aria-current="page"`).

isActive.description: Marks this item as the current page (sets `aria-current="page"`).

disabled.description: Disables interaction and dims the control.

indicatorWidth.description: Per-item override of the indicator width.

href.description: Render as a link (`<a>`) pointing at this URL.

asChild.description: Merge this component's props and styling onto its single child element instead of rendering its own (use with router `<Link>`s).

as.description: Render as a different element or component, e.g. `as={Link}`.

NavbarMenu.description: The collapsible mobile navigation drawer. Clicking any link inside it closes the menu; Escape also closes it.

NavbarToggle.description: Hamburger button that opens and closes `NavbarMenu`. Hidden on wide screens unless `display="always"`.

icon.description: Icon while closed. Defaults to a hamburger.

openIcon.description: Icon while open. Defaults to an X.

aria-label.description: Defines a string value that labels the current element.

display.description: `auto` shows the toggle only on small screens; `always` / `never` force it.

NumberInput.description:
A numeric field with stepper buttons. Typing is free-form; the value is
clamped to `min`/`max` and committed on blur or Enter. Arrow keys step.

onChange.description: Called with the committed (clamped, step-rounded) number.

step.description: Increment used by arrow keys and stepper buttons.

size.description: Height matching the Button of the same size (`sm` 30px, `md` 36px, `lg` 44px, `xl` 48px). Default `md`.

width.description: Width of the field (number = px, or any CSS length).

isFullWidth.description: Stretch to the container width. Default `false`.

unit.description: Unit label shown inside the field, e.g. `GB`.

label.description: Visible label, linked to the control for screen readers.

helperText.description: Hint shown under the control (hidden while `error` is set).

error.description: Error message shown under the control; also sets `aria-invalid`.

disabled.description: Disables interaction and dims the control.

name.description: Form field name, so the value is submitted with native forms.

id.description: Element id. Generated automatically when omitted (labels stay linked).

required.description: Marks the field as required (adds a * to the label and native validation).

placeholder.description: Text shown when there is no value.

onBlur.description: Called when the control loses focus (useful for form libraries).

aria-label.description: Accessible name when there is no visible label.

examples: <NumberInput label="Instances" min={1} max={20} value={count} onChange={setCount} />

Pagination.description:
Page navigation with first/prev/next/last, a page window with ellipses and
an optional page-size selector. `variant="simple"` swaps the page window for a
compact "Page 4 of 48" status between prev/next. Use `surface={false}` for flat pagination under a card grid.

pageSize.description: Rows per page (used for the "Showing x–y" summary).

onPageChange.description: Called with the 1-based page to show.

onPageSizeChange.description: Shows a "Rows per page" select when provided.

variant.description:
`full` (default): first/prev, numbered page window, next/last.
`simple`: prev/next with a "Page 4 of 48" status between them — for cards, feeds and tight spaces.

surface.description:
Draw the raised bar (padding, top border and background) that suits a table footer. Set `false` for
flat pagination under a grid of cards. Default `true`.

showFirstLast.description: Show the first/last page buttons. Default `true` for `full`, `false` for `simple`.

examples:
<Pagination currentPage={page} totalPages={12} onPageChange={setPage} totalItems={118} pageSize={10} />
<Pagination variant="simple" currentPage={page} totalPages={12} onPageChange={setPage} />

Popover.description:
Floating panel anchored to a trigger, for rich content such as details,
filters or small forms. Closes on outside click and Escape, and returns
focus to the trigger.

trigger.description: Element that toggles the popover. A plain node is wrapped in an unstyled button.

align.description: Horizontal alignment to the trigger. Default `start`.

position.description: Preferred side; flips when there isn't room. Default `bottom`.

onOpenChange.description: Called with the new open state.

aria-label.description: Accessible name of the panel.

container.description: Element to render the portal into. Defaults to `document.body`.

examples: <Popover trigger={<Button>Filters</Button>} content={<FilterForm />} />

Progress.description: A horizontal progress bar for determinate (`value`) or indeterminate work.

value.description: Current value (0 to `max`). Omit for an indeterminate bar.

label.description: Visible label, linked to the control for screen readers.

showValue.description: Show the percentage next to the label.

aria-label.description: Accessible name when there is no visible label.

examples: <Progress label="Uploading" value={42} showValue />

Prose.description:
Styles raw HTML content (headings, paragraphs, lists, quotes, images, tables, code)
from Markdown or a CMS, e.g. about pages, blog posts and policies.

size.description: Base text size. Default `base`. Accepts a breakpoint object, e.g. `{ base: 'base', lg: 'lg' }`.

maxWidth.description: Max line length. Default `68ch`; pass `none` to fill the container.

collapsible.description:
Collapse long text to its first `previewParagraphs` paragraphs with a "Read more" toggle. `true`
collapses on phones only (below 640px); `'always'` at every width; a breakpoint object chooses per
breakpoint, e.g. `{ base: true, lg: false }` collapses below 1024px. It is CSS only, so the first
paint is already right. The toggle only appears where the text collapses and there is more to show.
When set, the content and toggle render inside a `div.field-prose-collapsible` wrapper, which
receives `className` and `style`.

previewParagraphs.description: Paragraphs shown while collapsed (1–10); everything after the last one is hidden. Default `2`.

expandLabel.description: Label for expand button. Default `Read more`.

collapseLabel.description: Label for collapse button. Default `Show less`.

as.description: Element to render. Default `div`; use `article` for posts.

examples: <Prose as="article" dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: post.html }} />

RadioGroup.description:
A set of mutually exclusive options. Uses native radio inputs, so arrow
keys move the selection and the group submits with forms.

label.description: Visible label, linked to the control for screen readers.

onChange.description: Called with the new value whenever it changes.

disabled.description: Disables interaction and dims the control.

orientation.description: Stack options vertically (default) or lay them out in a row.

helperText.description: Hint shown under the control (hidden while `error` is set).

error.description: Error message shown under the control; also sets `aria-invalid`.

name.description: Form field name. Generated automatically if omitted.

required.description: Marks the field as required (adds a * to the label and native validation).

aria-label.description: Accessible name when there is no visible label.

examples:
<RadioGroup label="Plan" value={plan} onChange={setPlan} options={[
  { value: 'free', label: 'Free' },
  { value: 'pro', label: 'Pro', description: '$12 / month' },
]} />

Reveal.description:
Fades content in as it scrolls into view. Skipped entirely for users who prefer
reduced motion, and content stays visible if JavaScript has not run (SSR).

delay.description: Delay in ms, e.g. to stagger cards.

once.description: Animate only the first time it enters the viewport. Default `true`.

asChild.description: Apply reveal directly to the single child instead of creating a wrapper element.

fill.description: Stretch wrapper to 100% height of parent container (preserves equal-height grids).

as.description: Element to render. Default `div`.

Section.description:
A full-width page band with consistent vertical rhythm, an optional background
tone or image, and a centred container. The building block of marketing pages.
Give it an `id` to make it an in-page link target: anchors stop below a sticky `Navbar`
automatically (`--field-scroll-offset`, derived from `--field-navbar-height`).

tone.description:
Background band. `muted` / `raised` use theme surfaces, `accent` fills with the brand colour,
`inverse` flips to the opposite light/dark theme (e.g. a dark band on a light site).

spacing.description: Vertical padding; fluid, so it shrinks on small screens. Default `lg`.

container.description: Wraps children in a `Container` of this width. Pass `false` for full-bleed content. Default `xl`.

underNavbar.description:
Pull the section up under a transparent sticky `Navbar` (negative margin of `--field-navbar-height`, with the
same amount added to the top padding). Also tells `Navbar transparentOnTop="auto"` that a band sits under it.

backgroundImage.description: Cover image behind the content: a URL, or `{ src, srcSet, sizes, position, priority }`. It renders as an `` (object-fit cover), so `srcSet` picks the right file on phones and `priority` (for the hero) loads it first. The section switches to the dark theme (or the pair's `band` theme, see `createThemePair`) and adds `overlay`.

overlay.description: Darkness of the overlay over `backgroundImage`, 0 to 1. Default `0.55`.

as.description: Element to render. Default `section`.

examples:
<Section tone="muted" id="menu" aria-labelledby="menu-title">
  <Heading id="menu-title" display="sm">Our menu</Heading>
</Section>

SectionHeader.description:
Responsive header block for section introductions: eyebrow, title, lead text, and optional action.
On mobile, actions wrap underneath the title and description cleanly. It has no outer margin, so
space it with the parent's `gap` (e.g. a `Stack`).

eyebrow.description: Eyebrow / overline label displayed above the title (rendered as `Text variant="overline"`).

title.description: Primary section title, rendered with `Heading`, so it uses the theme's display font, weights and tracking.

display.description: `Heading` display size of the title. Default `sm`; pass `false` for the size `headingLevel` implies (levels 5 and 6 use level 4's).

headingId.description: `id` of the heading element, e.g. for the section's `aria-labelledby`. Other props go to the wrapper.

description.description: Optional lead or description paragraph (`Text size="lg" tone="secondary" measure`).

action.description: Call to action button or link, placed beside the header on wide screens and below on mobile.

align.description: Text alignment: `start` (default) or `center`, as on `Heading` and `Text`.

examples:
<Section aria-labelledby="archive-title">
  <Stack gap="$8">
    <SectionHeader
      eyebrow="Collections"
      title="Our Aircraft Archive"
      headingId="archive-title"
      description="Explore photographic history from RAF Snaith."
      action={<Button variant="outline">View all</Button>}
    />
    …
  </Stack>
</Section>

SegmentedControl.description:
A compact single-choice toggle (like a radio group styled as joined
buttons). Arrow keys move between options.

onChange.description: Called with the new value whenever it changes.

isFullWidth.description: Stretch segments to fill the container width.

aria-label.description: Accessible name for the group, e.g. "View mode".

disabled.description: Disables interaction and dims the control.

examples:
<SegmentedControl aria-label="Range" value={range} onChange={setRange}
  options={[{ value: '24h', label: '24h' }, { value: '7d', label: '7d' }]} />

Select.description:
A styled, accessible single-select dropdown (WAI-ARIA select-only combobox).
Supports arrow keys, Home/End, type-ahead and native form submission via `name`.

label.description: Visible label, linked to the control for screen readers.

onChange.description: Called with the selected option's value.

placeholder.description: Text shown when there is no value.

disabled.description: Disables interaction and dims the control.

helperText.description: Hint shown under the control (hidden while `error` is set).

error.description: Error message shown under the control; also sets `aria-invalid`.

size.description: Height matching the Button of the same size (`sm` 30px, `md` 36px, `lg` 44px, `xl` 48px). Without it the trigger is 40px tall.

name.description: Renders a hidden input so the value is submitted with native forms.

id.description: Element id. Generated automatically when omitted (labels stay linked).

required.description: Marks the field as required (adds a * to the label and native validation).

onBlur.description: Called when the control loses focus (useful for form libraries).

aria-label.description: Accessible name when no visible `label` is rendered.

container.description: Element to render the dropdown into. Defaults to `document.body`.

examples:
<Select label="Region" value={region} onChange={setRegion}
  options={[{ value: 'us-east-1', label: 'US East (N. Virginia)' }]} />

Sidebar.description:
Collapsible application sidebar. Compose with `SidebarHeader`,
`SidebarContent`, `SidebarGroup`, `SidebarItem`, `SidebarDropdown` and
`SidebarFooter`. Wrap in `SidebarProvider` to toggle it from elsewhere
(e.g. a `SidebarTrigger` in your header).

onCollapseChange.description: Called when the sidebar collapses or expands.

collapsedWidth.description: Width when collapsed to icons (number = px).

aria-label.description: Accessible name for the navigation landmark. Default "Sidebar".

examples:
<Sidebar>
  <SidebarHeader title="Acme" icon={<Logo />} />
  <SidebarContent>
    <SidebarGroup label="Compute">
      <SidebarItem icon={<Server size={16} />} label="Instances" isActive />
    </SidebarGroup>
  </SidebarContent>
</Sidebar>

SidebarDropdown.description: An expandable item revealing `SidebarSubItem`s on a tree line. Clicking it while collapsed expands the sidebar.

icon.description: Icon element, e.g. `<Server size={16} />` from lucide-react.

label.description: Visible label, linked to the control for screen readers.

badge.description: Small count or status shown on the right.

onToggle.description: Called with the new open state.

SidebarFooter.description: Bottom section (user menu, status). `collapsedChildren` replaces the content while collapsed.

collapsedChildren.description: Replacement content while the sidebar is collapsed (e.g. just an avatar).

SidebarGroup.description: A labelled group of sidebar items. The label hides when the sidebar is collapsed.

label.description: Visible label, linked to the control for screen readers.

SidebarHeader.description: Top section of the sidebar with title, subtitle, icon and the built-in collapse toggle. Pass `children` for a fully custom header.

icon.description: Icon element, e.g. `<Server size={16} />` from lucide-react.

SidebarItem.description: A navigation item with icon, label and badge. Shows a tooltip and keeps its accessible name when the sidebar is collapsed.

icon.description: Icon element, e.g. `<Server size={16} />` from lucide-react.

label.description: Visible label, linked to the control for screen readers.

badge.description: Small count or status shown on the right.

isActive.description: Marks this item as the current page (sets `aria-current="page"`).

disabled.description: Disables interaction and dims the control.

href.description: Render as a link (`<a>`) pointing at this URL.

asChild.description: Merge this component's props and styling onto its single child element instead of rendering its own (use with router `<Link>`s).

as.description: Render as a different element or component, e.g. `as={Link}`.

SidebarProvider.description: Shares collapsed state between a `Sidebar` and controls elsewhere (e.g. a `SidebarTrigger` in your header). Read it with `useSidebar()`.

onCollapseChange.description: Called when the sidebar collapses or expands.

SidebarSubItem.description: A nested link inside a `SidebarDropdown`, with optional description and badge.

label.description: Visible label, linked to the control for screen readers.

badge.description: Small count or status shown on the right.

isActive.description: Marks this item as the current page (sets `aria-current="page"`).

disabled.description: Disables interaction and dims the control.

href.description: Render as a link (`<a>`) pointing at this URL.

asChild.description: Merge this component's props and styling onto its single child element instead of rendering its own (use with router `<Link>`s).

as.description: Render as a different element or component, e.g. `as={Link}`.

SidebarTrigger.description: Standalone collapse/expand button for use outside the sidebar (inside `SidebarProvider`).

isCollapsed.description: Override the collapsed state (defaults to the sidebar context).

onToggle.description: Custom toggle handler (defaults to the sidebar context).

Skeleton.description: A shimmering placeholder shown while content loads. Hidden from assistive tech.

ratio.description: Aspect ratio, e.g. `16 / 9`, `1`, or `"4/3"`. When provided, height defaults to `auto`.

radius.description: Corner radius: a token name (`none`, `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`, `full`) or any CSS length. Default `sm`.

circle.description: Render a circle (`width` is used for both dimensions).

SkipLink.description:
"Skip to content" link for keyboard users. Hidden until focused; place it first in the page
and give your main landmark the matching id (`<main id="main">`). Focus is moved to the
target directly, so it also works with hash routers and targets that are not focusable.

href.description: Target of the main content, e.g. `#main`. Default `#main`.

Slider.description:
A range input with optional colour-coded threshold zones. Built on a native
`<input type="range">` for keyboard and screen-reader support.

label.description: Visible label, linked to the control for screen readers.

step.description: Increment used by arrow keys and stepper buttons.

onChange.description: Called with the new value whenever it changes.

zones.description: Colour-coded ranges, e.g. healthy / warning / critical thresholds.

showMarks.description: Show zone boundary values under the track.

glow.description: Soft glow around the fill and thumb.

disabled.description: Disables interaction and dims the control.

showValue.description: Show the current value in the header. Default `true`.

valueSuffix.description: Appended to the displayed value, e.g. `%` or ` GB`.

name.description: Form field name, so the value is submitted with native forms.

id.description: Element id. Generated automatically when omitted (labels stay linked).

required.description: Marks the field as required (adds a * to the label and native validation).

aria-label.description: Accessible name when there is no visible label.

examples:
<Slider label="CPU alarm" valueSuffix="%" value={cpu} onChange={setCpu}
  zones={[{ to: 60, color: 'success', label: 'Healthy' }, { to: 85, color: 'warning' }, { to: 100, color: 'danger' }]} />

Sparkline.description: A tiny inline trend line with no axes. Pair with a number in a `StatCard`.

color.description: Status keyword or any CSS colour.

filled.description: Fill the area under the line. Default `true`.

aria-label.description: Describe the trend for screen readers (otherwise the chart is decorative).

examples: <Sparkline data={[4, 6, 5, 9, 12]} color="success" aria-label="Requests trending up" />

Spinner.description: An animated loading indicator, announced as "Loading" by screen readers.

label.description: Text announced to screen readers. Default "Loading".

Stack.description: Vertical stack with consistent spacing between children.

gap.description: Space between children. Default 16px (`$4`). Accepts a breakpoint object.

align.description:
Horizontal alignment of children: `start`, `center`, `end`, `stretch` (default) or `baseline`.
Accepts a breakpoint object. With `stretch`,
direct `img`, `svg`, `video` and `canvas` children keep their own width so they are not distorted.

as.description: Element to render. Default `div`.

padding.description: Padding (number = px, `$4` = spacing token); accepts a breakpoint object.

hideBelow.description: Hide below this breakpoint (e.g. `hideBelow="md"` shows only from 768px).

hideFrom.description: Hide from this breakpoint up (e.g. `hideFrom="md"` shows only below 768px).

StatCard.description: A KPI tile: label, large value, optional trend delta and sparkline.

label.description: Visible label, linked to the control for screen readers.

delta.description: Change indicator. `up` is green and `down` red unless `invertTrendColors` is set.

icon.description: Icon element, e.g. `<Server size={16} />` from lucide-react.

subtitle.description: Small supporting text under the value.

chart.description: Visual under the value, e.g. a `<Sparkline>`.

examples:
<StatCard label="Monthly spend" value="$12,480" delta={{ value: '4.2%', trend: 'up' }}
  chart={<Sparkline data={spend} />} />

StatusDot.description: A coloured dot indicating health or connection state, optionally labelled.

pulse.description: Animated ring for "live" states. Respects reduced motion.

label.description: Visible label, linked to the control for screen readers.

examples: <StatusDot status="success" pulse label="Live" />

Stepper.description:
Progress through a multi-step flow. The current step is marked
`aria-current="step"`; completed steps can be revisited via `onStepClick`.

onStepClick.description: Makes completed steps clickable (to go back).

examples: <Stepper activeStep={1} steps={[{ id: 'a', title: 'Configure' }, { id: 'b', title: 'Review' }, { id: 'c', title: 'Launch' }]} />

Switch.description:
An on/off toggle for settings that apply immediately. Backed by a native
`<input type="checkbox" role="switch">`, so it is keyboard accessible,
labelled by its text and submits with forms.

label.description: Visible label, linked to the control for screen readers.

onChange.description: Called with the new state when toggled.

disabled.description: Disables interaction and dims the control.

examples: <Switch label="Auto-scaling" description="Add capacity under load" checked={on} onChange={setOn} />

Table.description:
Data table with sorting, row selection with bulk actions, expandable rows,
loading skeletons and an empty state. For full control, use the compound
parts (`TableHeader`, `TableBody`, `TableRow`, `TableHead`, `TableCell`) as
children instead of `columns` / `data`.

keyExtractor.description: Stable key for each row. Strongly recommended with selection or expansion. Defaults to the row index.

children.description: Compound mode: pass `TableHeader`/`TableBody`/... children instead of `columns`/`data`.

loadingRows.description: Number of skeleton rows while loading. Default 5.

stickyHeader.description: Keep the header row visible while the container scrolls (give the table a max height via `style`).

onRowClick.description: Called when a row is clicked (ignored for clicks on buttons, links and inputs inside the row).

onSortChange.description: Called when the user changes sorting. `sortKey` is `null` when sorting is cleared.

manualSorting.description: Data is already sorted (e.g. by the server); only report sort changes.

selectable.description: Add a checkbox column for row selection.

selectedKeys.description: Controlled selection. Omit to let the table manage selection itself.

onSelectionChange.description: Called with the selected row keys.

renderBulkActions.description: Toolbar shown above the table while rows are selected.

expandable.description: Add an expand toggle per row.

renderExpandedRow.description: Content shown under an expanded row.

examples:
<Table data={instances} keyExtractor={r => r.id} selectable
  columns={[
    { key: 'name', header: 'Name', sortable: true },
    { key: 'state', header: 'State', render: r => <Badge variant="success" dot>{r.state}</Badge> },
  ]} />

TableHead.description: Compound header cell. Set `sortable` + `sortOrder` + `onSort` for a sort button with `aria-sort`.

sortable.description: Render the header as a sort button.

sortOrder.description: Current sort direction for this column (`null` = unsorted).

onSort.description: Called when the sort button is clicked.

TableRow.description: Compound table row. `isSelected` highlights it; `onClick` makes it clickable.

TabPanel.description:
Content for one tab. Only renders while its tab is active (unless
`keepMounted`), and is labelled by its tab for screen readers.

id.description: Must match the `id` of a tab item.

keepMounted.description: Keep the panel mounted (hidden) when inactive, preserving its state. Default `false`.

Tabs.description:
Horizontal tabs. Arrow keys move between tabs, Home/End jump to the ends.
Render content with `<TabPanel id>` children, or read `activeId` yourself.

defaultActiveId.description: Initial tab when uncontrolled. Defaults to the first tab.

onChange.description: Called with the new value whenever it changes.

aria-label.description: Accessible name for the tab list.

children.description: Tab panels. Use `<TabPanel id="...">` so ARIA attributes are wired up.

examples:
<Tabs items={[{ id: 'overview', label: 'Overview' }, { id: 'logs', label: 'Logs' }]}>
  <TabPanel id="overview">…</TabPanel>
  <TabPanel id="logs">…</TabPanel>
</Tabs>

Terminal.description:
A terminal / log viewer window. Compose with `TerminalHeader`, `TerminalBody`
(containing `TerminalLine`s) and an optional interactive `TerminalPrompt`.

variant.description:
`window` (default): raised window chrome with dots, icon, level badges and a submit button.
`minimal`: flat panel for embedding in consoles and dashboards; the sub-components default
to no dots, no icon, no level badges and no submit button (each can be opted back in).

examples:
<Terminal height={320}>
  <TerminalHeader title="deploy.log" onClear={clear} />
  <TerminalBody>
    {logs.map(l => <TerminalLine key={l.id} level={l.level} timestamp={l.ts}>{l.text}</TerminalLine>)}
  </TerminalBody>
  <TerminalPrompt onSubmit={run} />
</Terminal>

Header, body and prompt are all optional, so a bare `<Terminal variant="minimal"><TerminalBody>…`
is a plain embedded log.

TerminalBody.description: Scrollable output area. Auto-scrolls to the newest line while `autoScroll` is on.

autoScroll.description: Scroll to the newest line when children change.

TerminalHeader.description: Window chrome with title and optional scroll-to-bottom, copy and clear actions.

subtitle.description: Secondary text next to the title.

icon.description: Icon before the title. Defaults to a terminal glyph in the `window` variant; pass `null` to hide it.

showControls.description: Show macOS-style window dots. Default `true` for `window`, `false` for `minimal`.

onClear.description: Shows a clear button when provided.

onCopyAll.description: Shows a copy button when provided.

onScrollToBottom.description: Shows a scroll-to-bottom button when provided.

TerminalLine.description: One log line with optional timestamp, level badge (`info`, `warn`, `error`, `success`, `debug`, `cmd`) and prefix.

level.description: Log level; sets the badge and text colour.

prefix.description: Text shown before the content, e.g. a service name.

showBadge.description: Show the level badge. Default `true` for `window`, `false` for `minimal` (the text colour still reflects the level).

TerminalPrompt.description: Interactive command input with ↑/↓ history. `onSubmit` receives the trimmed command.

path.description: Working directory shown in the prompt.

prompt.description: Replaces the `user:path$` label entirely, e.g. `">"` or `"$"`.

showSubmitButton.description: Show the submit button. Default `true` for `window`, `false` for `minimal`.

onChange.description: Called with the new value whenever it changes.

onSubmit.description: Called with the trimmed command on Enter.

placeholder.description: Text shown when there is no value.

disabled.description: Disables interaction and dims the control.

Text.description: Body text with size, tone and weight presets.

variant.description: Text style variant. `overline` renders compact uppercase tracked text for badges/eyebrows.

size.description: Text size. `xl` is a fluid lead/intro size for hero and section copy.

align.description: Text alignment; accepts a breakpoint object.

truncate.description: Truncate to a single line with an ellipsis.

measure.description: Limit the line length for readability: `true` = 66ch, a number = px (as on every Field size prop), or any CSS length such as `"60ch"`.

tabularNums.description: Tabular lining figures for numbers, timers, prices, and metrics.

as.description: Element to render. Default `p`; use `span` inside inline contexts.

examples:
<Text size="sm" tone="secondary">Last deployed 3 minutes ago</Text>
<Text size="xl" tone="secondary" align="center">Small-batch coffee, roasted on site.</Text>

TextArea.description: Multi-line text field. Shares label/helper/error behaviour with `TextInput`.

label.description: Visible label, linked to the control for screen readers.

helperText.description: Hint shown under the control (hidden while `error` is set).

error.description: Error message shown under the control; also sets `aria-invalid`.

isFullWidth.description: Stretch to the container width. Default `true`.

examples: <TextArea label="Description" rows={4} maxLength={500} />

TextInput.description:
Single-line text field with label, helper text, error state and adornments.
`ref`, `value`, `onChange` and every native `<input>` prop are forwarded, so
it works with React Hook Form, Formik, etc.

label.description: Visible label, associated with the input automatically.

helperText.description: Hint shown under the input (hidden while `error` is set).

error.description: Error message; also marks the input `aria-invalid`.

leftAdornment.description: Content inside the field before the text, e.g. a search icon.

rightAdornment.description: Content inside the field after the text, e.g. a unit or a clear button.

isFullWidth.description: Stretch to the container width. Default `true`.

size.description:
Height matching the Button of the same size (`sm` 30px, `md` 36px, `lg` 44px, `xl` 48px), so a field
and a button line up in a row. Without it the field is 40px tall.

htmlSize.description: The native `size` attribute (visible width in characters).

wrapperClassName.description: Class applied to the bordered input wrapper (`className` styles the same element).

examples: <TextInput label="Email" type="email" required helperText="We'll never share it." />

ThemeProvider.description:
Provides the active Field theme to every component below it.

With `scope="root"` (default) the theme's CSS variables are written to
`<html>`, so the whole page (including portals) is themed. With
`scope="container"` they are applied to a wrapper element instead, which
lets you render several themes side by side.

initialTheme.description: Start with a specific theme instead of a pair.

themePair.description: Dark/light theme pair to use. Defaults to the built-in Obsidian / Cobalt pair.

linkComponent.description:
Router link component used for internal `href`s by link-rendering components. It receives
`href` (never `to`): `next/link` works as is; for React Router or TanStack Router pass an
adapter that maps `href` to `to` (see the Routing guide). External URLs, `#` anchors and links
with `download` or a `target` other than `_self` render a plain `<a>` instead.

defaultMode.description: Initial mode. `'system'` follows the OS `prefers-color-scheme` setting. Default `'dark'`.

storageKey.description: When set, the chosen mode is saved to `localStorage` under this key and restored on load.

injectGlobalStyles.description: Write CSS variables to `<html>` when `scope="root"`. Default `true`.

scope.description: `root` themes the whole document; `container` themes only a wrapper element. Default `root`.

as.description: Wrapper element type (container scope, or root scope with className/style).

ThemeScope.description:
Applies a different theme (or mode) to a subtree, e.g. a light card inside
a dark page. Components inside - including portals such as tooltips and
modals opened from within - use the scoped theme.

themePair.description: Theme pair for this subtree (mode inherited unless `mode` is set).

mode.description: Force dark or light for this subtree, using the current pair.

asChild.description: Merge theme attributes and variables directly onto the child element without creating a wrapper div.

as.description: Render as a different element or component, e.g. `as={Link}`.

Timeline.description:
A vertical feed of events (deploys, audit logs, activity, history milestones).

Restyle it with CSS variables on the list (or any ancestor): `--field-timeline-marker-size`,
`-marker-border-width`, `-marker-color` (overrides every status), `-marker-bg`, `-rail-width`,
`-rail-color`, `-gap` (marker to content), `-item-gap`, `-time-color`, `-time-weight`,
`-time-width` (the `left` column) and `-marker-icon-color` (`markerVariant="solid"`).

markerSize.description: Marker diameter: `sm` 10px, `md` 16px (default), `lg` 28px (fits an icon), or a px number. Sets `--field-timeline-marker-size`.

timestampPosition.description: Where the timestamp renders: `inline` (beside the title), `top` (above the title) or `left` (a column left of the rail). Default `inline`.

markerVariant.description:
`ring` (default): an outlined marker in the status colour. `solid`: filled with the status colour, with
the icon in its contrast colour (`--field-timeline-marker-icon-color` overrides it). Use `markerSize="lg"`
for icons.

examples: <Timeline items={[{ id: '1', title: 'Deployed v2.4.0', timestamp: '2m ago', dateTime: '2026-10-12T09:30', status: 'success' }]} />

ToastProvider.description:
Hosts transient notifications. Wrap your app once, then call
`useToast().showToast(...)` anywhere below it.

position.description: Screen corner for the stack. Default `bottom-right`.

limit.description: Maximum toasts on screen; older ones are dropped. Default 5.

container.description: Element to render the portal into. Defaults to `document.body`.

examples:
const { showToast } = useToast();
showToast({ title: 'Saved', variant: 'success' });

Tooltip.description:
A short text label shown on hover or keyboard focus. The trigger is linked
with `aria-describedby`, and Escape dismisses it.

children.description: The element that triggers the tooltip on hover and focus.

position.description: Preferred side; flips when there is no room. Default `top`.

delay.description: Hover delay before showing, in ms. Default `200`.

disabled.description: Disable the tooltip without unmounting the trigger.

container.description: Element to render the portal into. Defaults to `document.body`.

examples: <Tooltip content="Copy to clipboard"><IconButton icon={<Copy />} aria-label="Copy" /></Tooltip>

TreeView.description:
A hierarchical list (file browser, resource tree). Keyboard: ↑/↓ move,
→ expands or enters, ← collapses or goes to the parent, Enter selects.

onSelect.description: Called when the item is chosen.

defaultExpandedIds.description: Initially expanded node ids when uncontrolled.

onExpandedChange.description: Called with the expanded node ids when a node is expanded or collapsed.

aria-label.description: Accessible name for the tree.

examples: <TreeView aria-label="Files" data={tree} selectedId={file} onSelect={n => setFile(n.id)} />

as.description: Semantic heading tag level

variant.description: Style variant. The component now uses a unified calligraphic facet drafting architecture.

trigger.description: Animation trigger mode: 'mount' (immediate), 'scroll' (on viewport entry), or 'manual'

intensity.description: Visual wireframe prominence: 'subtle' (muted ghosted hairline), 'medium', or 'vibrant' (neon HUD)

wireframeOpacity.description: Direct override for stroke opacity (0.0 to 1.0)

speed.description: Animation speed preset ('fast' | 'normal' | 'slow' | 'cinematic') or custom milliseconds per facet step

triangleSpeedMs.description: Milliseconds per individual facet draw (overrides speed preset if specified, default: 28ms)

leadLetterLag.description: Number of letters the wireframe leads ahead before trailing letters materialize into styled font (default: 2)

wireframeColor.description: Wireframe stroke/crease color (defaults to cyan blueprint accent #00d2ff)

fillColor.description: Solid fill color for standard words (defaults to var(--field-text-primary))

highlightWords.description: Array of words to highlight with accent color (like 'CRAFT' and 'EXPERIENCES')

highlightColor.description: Color for highlighted words (defaults to vibrant blue #2563eb)

once.description: Whether the animation should only play once

duration.description: Total animation duration override in seconds (optional)

onComplete.description: Callback fired when the entire heading animation finishes

UnfoldingHeading.description:
Display heading whose letters are drawn as a wireframe and then "materialise"
into solid type. The full text is always available to screen readers, and
the animation is skipped when the user prefers reduced motion.

as.description: Semantic heading tag level

variant.description: Style variant. The component now uses a unified calligraphic facet drafting architecture.

trigger.description: Animation trigger mode: 'mount' (immediate), 'scroll' (on viewport entry), or 'manual'

intensity.description: Visual wireframe prominence: 'subtle' (muted ghosted hairline), 'medium', or 'vibrant' (neon HUD)

wireframeOpacity.description: Direct override for stroke opacity (0.0 to 1.0)

speed.description: Animation speed preset ('fast' | 'normal' | 'slow' | 'cinematic') or custom milliseconds per facet step

triangleSpeedMs.description: Milliseconds per individual facet draw (overrides speed preset if specified, default: 28ms)

leadLetterLag.description: Number of letters the wireframe leads ahead before trailing letters materialize into styled font (default: 2)

wireframeColor.description: Wireframe stroke/crease color (defaults to cyan blueprint accent #00d2ff)

fillColor.description: Solid fill color for standard words (defaults to var(--field-text-primary))

highlightWords.description: Array of words to highlight with accent color (like 'CRAFT' and 'EXPERIENCES')

highlightColor.description: Color for highlighted words (defaults to vibrant blue #2563eb)

once.description: Whether the animation should only play once

duration.description: Total animation duration override in seconds (optional)

onComplete.description: Callback fired when the entire heading animation finishes

examples: <UnfoldingHeading as="h1" size="hero" text="Build faster" highlightWords={['faster']} trigger="scroll" />

VisuallyHidden.description:
Hides content visually while keeping it fully accessible to screen readers.
Use `below` (e.g. `below="sm"`) to hide labels on small mobile screens only.

below.description:
Only visually hide on screens narrower than this breakpoint.
On wider screens, the element renders visibly.

as.description: Element to render. Default `span`.

examples:
<VisuallyHidden>Current page</VisuallyHidden>
<VisuallyHidden below="sm">Basket ({count})</VisuallyHidden>

useAnchoredPosition.signature: (anchorRef: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>, floatingRef: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>, open: boolean, { placement, align, offset, matchWidth }?: AnchoredPositionOptions): { ...; }
useAnchoredPosition.description:
Positions a `position: fixed` floating element next to an anchor, keeping
it inside the viewport and following scroll/resize. Rendering the floating
element in a portal with this style avoids clipping by `overflow` parents.

useControllableState.signature: <T>({ value, defaultValue, onChange, }: { value?: T; defaultValue: T; onChange?: ((value: T) => void); }): [T, (next: T) => void]
useControllableState.description:
State that can be either controlled (`value` provided) or uncontrolled
(`defaultValue`), calling `onChange` in both cases.

useCookieConsent.signature: (storageKey?: string): { consent: CookieConsentRecord | null; hasConsent: (categoryId: string) => boolean; openPreferences: () => void; reset: () => void; }
useCookieConsent.description:
Read the visitor's saved cookie choices anywhere in the app, and reopen the
preferences panel (e.g. from a "Cookie settings" footer link).

useDismissableLayer.description:
Close a popover/menu/dialog on Escape or outside press. When several layers
are open (a select inside a modal), only the topmost one responds.

useFocusTrap.signature: (containerRef: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>, active: boolean, options?: { initialFocusRef?: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>; restoreFocus?: boolean; }): void
useFocusTrap.description:
Trap Tab focus inside `containerRef` while active, move focus into it on
open, and restore focus to the previously focused element on close.

useIsomorphicLayoutEffect.description: `useLayoutEffect` on the client, `useEffect` on the server (avoids SSR warnings).

useLinkComponent.description: Returns the router link component provided to `<ThemeProvider linkComponent={...}>`, if any.

useMediaQuery.description: Track a CSS media query. Returns `defaultValue` during SSR and the first render.

usePortalThemeProps.signature: (extraClassName?: string, style?: CSSProperties): { className: string; 'data-field-theme': string; 'data-theme': "dark" | "light"; style: { accentColor?: AccentColor; ... 855 more ...; glyphOrientationVertical?: GlyphOrientationVertical; }; }
usePortalThemeProps.description:
Props for the root element of anything rendered into a portal (modals,
tooltips, toasts, popovers).

Portals escape the DOM subtree of a container-scoped `<ThemeProvider>` /
`<ThemeScope>`, so they would otherwise lose the theme's CSS variables.
When the nearest provider is container-scoped, the variables are inlined
onto the portal root; with root scope they are already on `<html>`.

usePrefersReducedMotion.description: True when the user asked the OS to reduce motion.
